terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The shell command to execute. Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is `-1`. Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

reset.description: If True, reset the terminal by creating a new session. Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive. Note that all previously set environment variables and session state will be lost after reset. Cannot be used with is_input=True.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.


Your current working directory is: /workspace
When exploring project structure, start with this directory instead of the root filesystem.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory.

function.description:
Use the tool to think about something. It will not obtain new information or make any changes to the repository, but just log the thought. Use it when complex reasoning or brainstorming is needed.

Common use cases:
1. When exploring a repository and discovering the source of a bug, call this tool to brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug, and assess which change(s) are likely to be simplest and most effective.
2. After receiving test results, use this tool to brainstorm ways to fix failing tests.
3. When planning a complex refactoring, use this tool to outline different approaches and their tradeoffs.
4. When designing a new feature, use this tool to think through architecture decisions and implementation details.
5. When debugging a complex issue, use this tool to organize your thoughts and hypotheses.

The tool simply logs your thought process for better transparency and does not execute any code or make changes.

* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.

  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.

  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs

  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`

    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.

   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

USER_CONTEXT: Migrate first-party jscodeshift 17.4.0 (commit e71f63dba4f60e39944f5ef1e74a36fbdd317e1e) JS→Rust, preserving all externally observable behavior. Scope: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities. Preserve package-root export (`index.js` → `src/core`) and direct jscodeshift compatibility. Host existing JS transforms.

TASK_TRACKING:
- MAP-01: Catalog first-party JS surface (CLI/args/discovery/ignore/runner/workers/core/collections/matching/templates/parsers/utils) — IN_PROGRESS

COMPLETED:
- Confirmed snapshot provenance: facebook/jscodeshift @ e71f63d / 17.4.0 under `/workspace/codebase` (no git metadata/deps)
- Read INSTRUCTION.md, UPSTREAM.md, README.md (partial), package.json
- Cataloged entrypoints: `bin/jscodeshift.js` (CLI), `bin/jscodeshift.sh` (thin wrapper → jscodeshift.js), `index.js` (`module.exports = require('./src/core')`)
- Cataloged runner stack: `src/Runner.js`, `src/Worker.js`, `src/argsParser.js`, `src/ignoreFiles.js`
- Cataloged core API: `src/core.js`, `src/Collection.js`, `src/matchNode.js`, `src/template.js`, `src/getParser.js`
- Cataloged collections barrel: `src/collections/index.js` exports Node, JSXElement, VariableDeclarator
- Noted sample transform `sample/reverse-identifiers.js` and `utils/requirePackage.js`
- Listed first-party tree (bin/, parser/, src/, sample/, docs/, test/, recipes/)
- AGENTS.md does not exist at /workspace/AGENTS.md

PENDING:
- Finish MAP-01 remaining first-party sources (parser adapters, collections implementations, utils, CLI args details)
- Design Rust/JS split (CLI, workers, JS transform bridge)
- Begin Rust port of cataloged surface

CURRENT_STATE:
- Working dir: /workspace
- Mapping phase: agent is reading first-party sources to design Rust/JS split against the real public surface

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.


Your current working directory is: /workspace
When exploring project structure, start with this directory instead of the root filesystem.

4. When designing a new feature, use this tool to think through architecture decisions and implementation details.
5. When debugging a complex issue, use this tool to organize your thoughts and hypotheses.

The tool simply logs your thought process for better transparency and does not execute any code or make changes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

Scope: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities. Preserve package-root export (`index.js` → `src/core`) and direct jscodeshift compatibility. Host existing JS transforms.

TASK_TRACKING:
- MAP-01: Catalog first-party JS surface (CLI/args/file discovery/ignore/runner/workers/core API/collections/matching/templates/parsers/package utils) — IN_PROGRESS (core sources read; Rust/JS split not yet designed)

COMPLETED:
- Read remaining first-party sources for MAP-01 catalog
- Confirmed toolchain: rustc/cargo 1.98.1, Node v22.23.2 (+16.20.2)

PENDING:
- Finish MAP-01 catalog (harness contract / public surface notes)
- Design Rust/JS split around transform hosting
- Implement Rust port preserving observable behavior

CURRENT_STATE:
First-party surface mapped:
- CLI: `bin/jscodeshift.js` → `src/Runner.js`
- Args: `src/argsParser.js`
- Ignore: `src/ignoreFiles.js` (picomatch, gitignore-style)
- Runner/workers: `src/Runner.js` (child_process, picocolors, graceful-fs), `src/Worker.js` (EventEmitter, neo-async)
- Core API: `index.js` re-exports `src/core.js`; `src/Collection.js` (recast)
- Matching/templates: `src/matchNode.js`, `src/template.js`
- Collections: Node, JSXElement, VariableDeclarator, ImportDeclaration (`src/collections/index.js`)
- Utils: intersection, union, once; `utils/requirePackage.js`
- Parsers: babel5Compat, babylon, flow, ts, tsx + tsOptions; `src/getParser.js`
- Package: name jscodeshift, version 17.4.0, main `index.js`
- Tests: `bin/__tests__`, `src/__tests__` (+snapshots), `src/__testfixtures__`, `src/utils/__tests__`

CODE_STATE:
No Rust crate yet. JS tree intact under /workspace/codebase. Agent next: design Rust/JS split so existing JS transforms remain hosted.

DEPS (JS, to preserve/replace): recast, @babel/parser, flow-parser, picomatch, picocolors, graceful-fs, neo-async, child_process

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

- MAP-02: Identify public exports, CLI flags, and compatibility constraints — PENDING
- DES-01: Design Rust/JS split that hosts existing transforms — PENDING
- IMPL: Implement Rust equivalents preserving observable behavior — PENDING
- VERIFY: Verify CLI/API compatibility and hosted JS transforms — PENDING

COMPLETED: Inspected package metadata, README (API + ignore rules), UPSTREAM.md, INSTRUCTION.md, CLI entrypoints, and first-party sources: bin/jscodeshift.{js,sh}, src/{argsParser,ignoreFiles,Runner,Worker,core,getParser,Collection,matchNode,template}.js, utils/requirePackage.js, index.js, package.json, parser adapters, sample/reverse-identifiers.js. - API: index.js → src/core.js (Collection, collections, getParser, template)

- Utils: src/ignoreFiles.js (picomatch gitignore), src/argsParser.js, utils/requirePackage.js

DEPS: recast, picomatch, picocolors, graceful-fs, neo-async, child_process workers

I still need the remaining first-party internals, tests, and setup files before I can lock the Rust/JS split.

USER_CONTEXT: Migrate first-party jscodeshift 17.4.0 (commit e71f63dba4f60e39944f5ef1e74a36fbdd317e1e) JS→Rust, preserving all externally observable behavior. Scope: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities. Preserve package-root export (`index.js` → `src/core`) and direct jscodeshift compatibility. Host existing JS transforms. JS stays only as the transform host.

TASK_TRACKING:
- MAP-01: Catalog first-party JS surface (CLI/args/discovery/ignore/runner/workers/core/collections/matching/templates/parsers/package utils) — IN PROGRESS
- DES-01: Design Rust/JS split around public surface — PENDING (blocked on MAP-01)

COMPLETED:
- Cataloged collections: `src/collections/index.js` exports Node, JSXElement, VariableDeclarator (+ ImportDeclaration)
- Cataloged collection impls: Node.js, JSXElement.js, VariableDeclarator.js, ImportDeclaration.js (all extend Collection/NodeCollection; use matchNode, once, assert)
- Cataloged utils: intersection.js (Set-based), union.js (Set-based), once.js (lodash-once replica)
- Cataloged parsers: babel5Compat.js, babylon.js (@babel/parser), flow.js (flow-parser), ts.js, tsx.js, tsOptions.js (shared TS/TSX options)
- Cataloged package surface: package.json (name jscodeshift, version 17.4.0, main index.js), index.js (re-exports ./src/core), bin/jscodeshift.js (requires ../src/Runner.js), bin/jscodeshift.sh (requires ./jscodeshift.js)
- Cataloged src/argsParser.js (throwError with exitCode/helpText), src/ignoreFiles.js (picomatch gitignore-style matchers)
- Read UPSTREAM.md (snapshot of facebook/jscodeshift @ e71f63d, no git metadata/deps), INSTRUCTION.md, README.md (testUtils.applyTransform API), repo tree

PENDING:
- Finish cataloging remaining first-party internals: Runner, workers, core API, matchNode, templates, file discovery, testUtils, package utilities
- Lock Rust/JS split: CLI/runner/ignore → Rust; JS only as transform host
- Implement migration

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

The tool simply logs your thought process for better transparency and does not execute any code or make changes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

- Create rust/ source directory
- Implement Rust crate: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers
- Port core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities

- Implementation not started beyond Cargo.toml

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

USER_CONTEXT: Migrate first-party jscodeshift 17.4.0 (commit e71f63dba4f60e39944f5ef1e74a36fbdd317e1e) JS→Rust, preserving all externally observable behavior. Scope: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities. Preserve package-root export (`index.js` → `src/core`) and direct jscodeshift compatibility. Host existing JS transforms. JS stays only as the transform host.

TASK_TRACKING:
- MAP-01: Catalog first-party surface, tests, and existing Rust/bridge scaffolding — IN_PROGRESS
- IMPL-01: Implement Rust CLI/runner/core + JS transform host — PENDING

COMPLETED:
- Mapped CLI (`bin/jscodeshift.js`, `bin/jscodeshift.sh`), package.json (v17.4.0, main: index.js), Cargo.toml (bin path rust/main.rs — file missing)
- Mapped core: `src/core.js`, `src/Collection.js`, `src/collections/Node.js`, `src/Worker.js`, `src/Runner.js`, `src/argsParser.js`, `src/ignoreFiles.js`, `src/getParser.js`
- Mapped parsers: babel5Compat, babylon, flow, ts, tsx, tsOptions
- Mapped utils: intersection.js, once.js, union.js, requirePackage.js
- Mapped sample transform: `sample/reverse-identifiers.js`
- Cataloged runtime: node v22.23.2, recast 0.23.11, babel 7.29.6, flow 0.237.2; DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS [".js",".jsx",".es6",".es",".mjs",".cjs"]; defaultExtensions cjs,es,es6,js,jsx,mjs,ts,tsx
- Confirmed empty `bridge/` and `app-setup/`; `dist/` has compiled JS; UPSTREAM.md + INSTRUCTION.md read

PENDING:
- Finish remaining module/test/harness catalog (MAP-01)
- Implement missing rust/main.rs and full Rust port (IMPL-01)
- Preserve index.js → src/core export and JS transform hosting

CURRENT_STATE: Exploring remaining contracts (color/picocolors, version, package details). rust/main.rs does not exist. JS source is the transform host; Rust crate must own CLI/runner/core.

CODE_STATE:
- Cargo.toml: package jscodeshift 17.4.0, bin jscodeshift → rust/main.rs (MISSING)
- index.js: module.exports = require('./src/core')
- Parsers via getParser switch: babylon, flow, ts, tsx, babel
- Runner uses child_process, picocolors, graceful-fs
- Worker uses EventEmitter, neo-async, graceful-fs
- ignoreFiles uses picomatch for gitignore-style patterns

DEPS: regex, serde, serde_json (Cargo.toml); JS: recast, @babel/parser, flow-parser, picocolors, picomatch, neo-async, graceful-fs

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Snapshot without git metadata; no Rust implementation started
I'll keep cataloging the remaining CLI, runner, and worker contracts so the Rust port can match the original behavior.

Scope: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities. Preserve package-root export (`index.js` → `src/core`) and direct jscodeshift compatibility. Host existing JS transforms. JS stays only as the transform host.

TASK_TRACKING:
- MAP-01: Catalog first-party JS surface (CLI, runner, workers, core, collections, match/template, parsers, package utils) — IN PROGRESS (most modules read; parsers/tests/utils still incomplete)

COMPLETED:
- Mapped CLI/runner/core entrypoints and collections/match/template surface
- Captured CLI status color codes and write-file-atomic contract
- Inspected env (Cargo/Node) and existing Cargo.toml scaffolding

PENDING:
- Finish mapping parsers, tests, remaining utils
- Implement Rust CLI + JS transform host matching original behavior
- Port runner/workers, file discovery, ignore rules, core API, collections, match/templates, parser adapters

CURRENT_STATE:
- Snapshot under `/workspace/codebase`; no git metadata
- `index.js` re-exports `./src/core`; bins: `bin/jscodeshift.js` (+ `.sh` shim)
- Collections: Node, JSXElement, VariableDeclarator, ImportDeclaration
- Parsers present: babylon, babel5Compat, flow, ts, tsx, tsOptions
- CLI statuses: OKK/NOC/SKIP/ERR/REP + colored summary (errors/unmodified/ok/Stats/dry)
- CARGO_HOME=/workspace/.cargo-home, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/workspace/.cargo-target (empty); Node 22
- Agent next: finish remaining contracts, then implement Rust CLI + JS transform host

CODE_STATE:
- `package.json`: name=jscodeshift, version=17.4.0, main=index.js
- `Cargo.toml`: bin `jscodeshift` → `rust/main.rs`; deps regex, serde, serde_json; edition 2021; publish=false
- Key JS: `src/{core,Collection,Runner,Worker,argsParser,ignoreFiles,getParser,matchNode,template}.js`, `src/collections/*`
- File writes via `write-file-atomic`; ignore via picomatch/gitignore-style; workers use neo-async + graceful-fs

DEPS:
- JS runtime: recast, picocolors, picomatch, graceful-fs, neo-async, write-file-atomic, imurmurhash, signal-exit
- Rust declared only: regex, serde, serde_json
- JS remains transform host

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Snapshot only (UPSTREAM.md); no repo/branch/PR; rust/main.rs referenced but not yet inspected/implemented
I'll finish mapping the remaining first-party contracts, then implement the Rust CLI and JS transform host against that surface.

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

Security risk levels for actions.

Based on OpenHands security risk levels but adapted for agent-sdk.
Integer values allow for easy comparison and ordering.

summary.description: A concise summary (approximately 10 words) describing what this specific action does. Focus on the key operation and target. Example: 'List all Python files in current directory'

command.description: The shell command to execute. Can be empty string to view additional logs when the previous exit code is `-1`. Can be a special key name when `is_input` is True: `C-c` (Ctrl+C), `C-d` (Ctrl+D/EOF), `C-z` (Ctrl+Z), or any `C-<letter>` for Ctrl sequences; navigation keys `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, `PGDN`; and `TAB`, `ESC`, `BS` (Backspace), `ENTER`. You can only execute one command at a time. Use the platform-appropriate shell syntax described in the tool description when chaining commands.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

timeout.description: Optional. Sets a maximum time limit (in seconds) for running the command. If the command takes longer than this limit, you’ll be asked whether to continue or stop it. If you don’t set a value, the command will instead pause and ask for confirmation when it produces no new output for 30 seconds. Use a higher value if the command is expected to take a long time (like installation or testing), or if it has a known fixed duration (like sleep).

reset.description: If True, reset the terminal by creating a new session. Use this only when the terminal becomes unresponsive. Note that all previously set environment variables and session state will be lost after reset. Cannot be used with is_input=True.

function.name: file_editor
function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.


Your current working directory is: /workspace
When exploring project structure, start with this directory instead of the root filesystem.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory.

file_text.description: Required parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created.

If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

function.name: think
function.description:
Use the tool to think about something. It will not obtain new information or make any changes to the repository, but just log the thought. Use it when complex reasoning or brainstorming is needed.

Common use cases:
1. When exploring a repository and discovering the source of a bug, call this tool to brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug, and assess which change(s) are likely to be simplest and most effective.
2. After receiving test results, use this tool to brainstorm ways to fix failing tests.
3. When planning a complex refactoring, use this tool to outline different approaches and their tradeoffs.
4. When designing a new feature, use this tool to think through architecture decisions and implementation details.
5. When debugging a complex issue, use this tool to organize your thoughts and hypotheses.

The tool simply logs your thought process for better transparency and does not execute any code or make changes.

function.description:
Execute a shell command in the terminal within a persistent shell session.


### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.
* Persistent session: Environment variables, virtual environments, and
  working directory changes persist across commands.
* Soft timeout: Commands pause for confirmation after 10 seconds without
  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.
* Shell options: Do NOT use `set -e`, `set -eu`, or `set -euo pipefail`.
  The runtime may not support them reliably.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs
  - Send text to STDIN of the running process
  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

### Output Handling
* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

### Terminal Reset
* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.
* Resetting the terminal clears environment variables, working directory
  changes, and running processes.

is_input.description: If True, the command is an input to the running process. If False, the command is executed in the terminal session. Default is False.

function.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files in plain-text format
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a text file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

2. UNIQUENESS: The `old_str` must uniquely identify a single instance in the file:
   - Include sufficient context before and after the change point (3-5 lines recommended)
   - If not unique, the replacement will not be performed

3. REPLACEMENT: The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that replace the `old_str`. Both strings must be different.

Remember: when making multiple file edits in a row to the same file, you should prefer to send all edits in a single message with multiple calls to this tool, rather than multiple messages with a single call each.

1. When exploring a repository and discovering the source of a bug, call this tool to brainstorm several unique ways of fixing the bug, and assess which change(s) are likely to be simplest and most effective.

USER_CONTEXT: Migrate first-party jscodeshift 17.4.0 (commit e71f63dba4f60e39944f5ef1e74a36fbdd317e1e) JS→Rust, preserving all externally observable behavior. Scope: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities. Preserve package-root export (`index.js` → `src/core`) and direct jscodeshift compatibility. Host existing JS transforms. JS stays only as the transform host.

TASK_TRACKING:
- MAP-01: Catalog first-party modules and their public contracts — IN_PROGRESS
- IMPL-01: Implement Rust CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules — PENDING
- IMPL-02: Implement Rust runner/workers + JS transform host — PENDING
- IMPL-03: Port core API, collections, matching, templates, parsers — PENDING
- VERIFY-01: Preserve package-root export and jscodeshift compatibility — PENDING

COMPLETED:
- Cataloged CLI entry points: `bin/jscodeshift.js` (shebang node, requires `../src/Runner.js`), `bin/jscodeshift.sh` (requires `./jscodeshift.js`)
- Cataloged `src/argsParser.js` (throwError with helpText, exit codes)
- Cataloged `src/Runner.js` (child_process, picocolors, graceful-fs)
- Cataloged `src/Worker.js` (EventEmitter, neo-async, graceful-fs)
- Cataloged `src/core.js` (Collection, collections, getParser)
- Cataloged `src/ignoreFiles.js` (picomatch, gitignore-style patterns)
- Cataloged `src/getParser.js` (switch: babylon and others)
- Cataloged `src/Collection.js` (forEach, some, typed method registration via astTypes)
- Cataloged `src/collections/Node.js` (Collection, matchNode, once)
- Cataloged parsers: `babel5Compat.js`, `babylon.js`, `flow.js`, `ts.js`, `tsx.js`, `tsOptions.js`
- Cataloged utils: `requirePackage.js`, `intersection.js`, `union.js`, `once.js`
- Cataloged sample transform: `sample/reverse-identifiers.js`
- Read `package.json` (name jscodeshift, version 17.4.0, main index.js)
- Read `Cargo.toml` (bin jscodeshift → rust/main.rs; deps: regex, serde, serde_json)

PENDING:
- Finish remaining first-party module catalog (MAP-01)
- Implement Rust CLI / runner / JS transform host
- Port core API, collections, matching, templates, parsers
- Preserve package-root export and compatibility

CURRENT_STATE:
- Workspace: /workspace/codebase (jscodeshift 17.4.0)
- Cargo.toml exists with rust/main.rs as binary entry; rust/ sources not yet created
- dist/ has compiled JS (Collection.js, Runner.js, Worker.js)
- bin/__tests__/ is empty
- /workspace/AGENTS.md does not exist
- Agent is cataloging source contracts before implementing Rust

CODE_STATE:
- package.json main: index.js → src/core
- Rust bin path: rust/main.rs (not yet implemented)
- JS transform host must remain for existing transforms

DEPS:
- JS: @babel/parser, flow-parser, picomatch, picocolors, graceful-fs, neo-async, recast/ast-types
- Rust (declared): regex 1, serde 1 (derive), serde_json 1

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: First-party snapshot at commit e71f63dba4f60e39944f5ef1e74a36fbdd317e1e, version 17.4.0
I'll continue cataloging remaining first-party modules and inspect the existing setup so the Rust port can match the original contracts.

### Command Execution
* One command at a time: You can only execute one shell command at a time.
  If you need to run multiple commands sequentially, use `&&` or `;`.

  working directory changes persist across commands.

  new output unless you provide a longer `timeout`.

### Long-running Commands
* For commands that may run indefinitely, run them in the background and
  redirect output to a file, e.g. `python3 app.py > server.log 2>&1 &`.
* For long-running commands, set the `timeout` parameter accordingly.
* If a command returns exit code `-1`, it hit the soft timeout and is
  still running. With `is_input=true`, you can:
  - Send empty `command` to retrieve additional logs

  - Send control commands like `C-c`, `C-d`, or `C-z`
  - Send navigation keys like `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TAB`,
    `ESC`, `BS`, `HOME`, `END`, `PGUP`, and `PGDN`
  - Send any `C-<letter>` Ctrl sequence such as `C-a`, `C-e`, or `C-l`

### Best Practices
* Verify a parent directory exists before creating files or directories.
* Prefer absolute paths and avoid excessive use of `cd`.

* Large output may be truncated before being returned.

* Set `reset=true` to create a fresh terminal session if the current one
  becomes unresponsive.

  changes, and running processes.

* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* The `undo_edit` command will revert the last edit made to the file at `path`
* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.


Before using this tool:
1. Use the view tool to understand the file's contents and context
2. Verify the directory path is correct (only applicable when creating new files):
   - Use the view tool to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

When making edits:
   - Ensure the edit results in idiomatic, correct code
   - Do not leave the code in a broken state
   - Always use absolute file paths (starting with /)

CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:

1. EXACT MATCHING: The `old_str` parameter must match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the file, including all whitespace and indentation. The tool will fail if `old_str` matches multiple locations or doesn't match exactly with the file content.

message.content:
USER_CONTEXT: Migrate first-party jscodeshift 17.4.0 (commit e71f63dba4f60e39944f5ef1e74a36fbdd317e1e) JS→Rust, preserving all externally observable behavior. Scope: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities. Preserve package-root export (`index.js` → `src/core`) and direct jscodeshift compatibility. Host existing JS transforms. JS stays only as the transform host.

TASK_TRACKING:
- MAP-01: Catalog first-party JS surface and contracts — IN_PROGRESS

COMPLETED: Inspected rust/ and bridge/ (empty stubs). Read index.js (re-exports src/core), package.json (v17.4.0, main: index.js), Cargo.toml (bin rust/main.rs, deps regex/serde/serde_json), INSTRUCTION.md, README.md.

PENDING: Finish cataloging remaining first-party modules (CLI, args, runner, workers, parsers, collections, templates, matchNode). Begin Rust port of CLI/args/file-discovery.

CURRENT_STATE: Cataloging first-party surface. Key files identified:
- bin/jscodeshift.js → Runner
- src/: argsParser.js, Runner.js, Worker.js, ignoreFiles.js, core.js, getParser.js, Collection.js, matchNode.js, template.js
- src/collections/: index.js, Node.js, JSXElement.js, VariableDeclarator.js, ImportDeclaration.js
- src/utils/: once.js, intersection.js, union.js
- utils/requirePackage.js
Workspace: rust/ and bridge/ empty; Cargo.toml already wired to rust/main.rs.

CODE_STATE:
- index.js: module.exports = require('./src/core')
- Cargo.toml: package jscodeshift 17.4.0, bin path rust/main.rs
- rust/ and bridge/ directories empty
- JS transform host must remain; Rust owns CLI/runner/core

DEPS: regex, serde, serde_json (Cargo.toml); JS still uses recast, picomatch, graceful-fs, neo-async, picocolors, babylon parsers

VERSION_CONTROL_STATUS: Source tree at jscodeshift 17.4.0; no Rust implementation commits yet
I have a solid picture of the first-party surface. Next I’ll catalog the remaining CLI, runner, and test contracts so the Rust port can match them exactly.

Scope: CLI, args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities. Preserve package-root export (`index.js` → `src/core`) and direct jscodeshift compatibility. Host existing JS transforms. JS stays only as the transform host.

TASK_TRACKING:
- MAP-01: Catalog first-party surface (CLI, runner, workers, core, collections, parsers, utils, tests) — IN_PROGRESS
- IMPL pending after mapping: CLI/args, file discovery, ignore rules, runner, workers, core API, collections, node matching, templates, parser adapters, package utilities

COMPLETED:
- Explored parser/, bin/, sample/, src/, src/utils/, src/__tests__, bin/__tests__, repo root
- Read Collection.js (forEach/some + typed method registration), all parser adapters, jscodeshift.sh, reverse-identifiers sample, once/intersection/union, argsParser.js, Runner.js, Worker.js, core.js, getParser.js, ignoreFiles.js, matchNode.js, template.js, INSTRUCTION.md

- Finish catalog of remaining first-party modules (collections/*, tests/snapshots, existing Rust/bridge stubs via Cargo.toml)
- Design Rust CLI + JS transform-host to match original contracts
- Implement port; preserve observable CLI/API behavior

CURRENT_STATE:
- Repo root already has Cargo.toml (Rust scaffolding present)
- CLI: `bin/jscodeshift.sh` shebang+`require('./jscodeshift.js')`; args via `src/argsParser.js` (`throwError(exitCode, message, helpText)`)
- Runner: `src/Runner.js` uses child_process, picocolors, graceful-fs
- Worker: `src/Worker.js` EventEmitter + neo-async + graceful-fs
- Core: `src/core.js` wires Collection, collections, getParser
- Collection: path-based; `forEach` binds callback to path; typed methods via `CPt[methodName].typedRegistrations` + `astTypes.getSupertypeNames` (supertypes set false)
- getParser switch includes babylon (+ others in file)

- ignoreFiles: picomatch + gitignore-style glob approximation
- matchNode: hasOwn-bound own-property matching
- template: recast builders/namedTypes
- Utils: once (lodash replica); intersection/union via Set
- Sample transform: `transformer(file, api)` reverses identifier names
- Tests: src/__tests__ (snapshots), bin/__tests__, parser/__tests__, sample/__tests__
- Agent still mapping; no Rust implementation started this session

- JS sources intact under /workspace/codebase/{bin,parser,sample,src}
